class TestInitializeDimensionWeights:

            strategy_names=["semantic"], learning_rate=0.1

    def test_init_empty_strategies(self):

            "Empty strategy list should produce empty logits dict"

class TestGetNormalizedWeights:
    """Tests for get_normalized_weights (softmax over logits)."""

    def test_uniform_logits_equal_weights(self, uniform_weights):
        """Uniform logits (all 0.0) produce equal weights 1/N."""
        result = get_normalized_weights(uniform_weights)
        n = 3
        for strategy, weight in result.items():
            assert weight == pytest.approx(1.0 / n, abs=1e-9), \
                f"Expected 1/{n} for '{strategy}', got {weight}"
        assert sum(result.values()) == pytest.approx(1.0, abs=1e-9)

    def test_unequal_logits_ordering(self, biased_weights):
        """Higher logit → higher weight, weights sum to 1.0, all in (0,1)."""
        result = get_normalized_weights(biased_weights)
        assert sum(result.values()) == pytest.approx(1.0, abs=1e-9), \
            "Weights must sum to 1.0"
        assert result["semantic"] > result["technical"] > result["social"], \
            "Higher logit should yield higher weight"
        for w in result.values():
            assert 0.0 < w < 1.0, f"Each weight should be in (0, 1), got {w}"

    def test_extra_strategies_default_logit(self):
        """Requesting strategies not in logits treats them as logit 0.0."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(strategy_names=["semantic"])
        w.logits["semantic"] = 1.0
        result = get_normalized_weights(w, strategies=["semantic", "technical"])
        assert "semantic" in result and "technical" in result, \
            "Both strategies must be present"
        assert result["semantic"] > result["technical"], \
            "semantic (logit 1.0) should have higher weight than technical (logit 0.0)"
        assert sum(result.values()) == pytest.approx(1.0, abs=1e-9)

    def test_empty_logits_empty_result(self, empty_weights):
        """Empty logits with no strategies parameter returns empty dict."""
        result = get_normalized_weights(empty_weights)
        assert result == {} or len(result) == 0, \
            "Empty logits should produce empty normalized weights"

    def test_single_strategy_weight_one(self):
        """Single strategy always gets weight 1.0 regardless of logit value."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(strategy_names=["semantic"])
        w.logits["semantic"] = 5.0
        result = get_normalized_weights(w)
        assert result["semantic"] == pytest.approx(1.0, abs=1e-9)

    def test_numerical_stability_extreme_logits(self):
        """Very large logit differences handled without overflow or NaN."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(
            strategy_names=["semantic", "technical"]
        )
        w.logits["semantic"] = 1000.0
        w.logits["technical"] = 0.0
        result = get_normalized_weights(w)
        for v in result.values():
            assert math.isfinite(v), f"All weights must be finite, got {v}"
        assert result["semantic"] == pytest.approx(1.0, abs=1e-6), \
            "Dominant logit should have weight ≈ 1.0"
        assert result["technical"] == pytest.approx(0.0, abs=1e-6)
        assert sum(result.values()) == pytest.approx(1.0, abs=1e-9)

    def test_translation_invariance(self):
        """Shifting all logits by same constant does not change weights."""
        w_a = initialize_dimension_weights(strategy_names=["s", "t"])
        w_a.logits["s"] = 1.0
        w_a.logits["t"] = 2.0

        w_b = initialize_dimension_weights(strategy_names=["s", "t"])
        w_b.logits["s"] = 101.0
        w_b.logits["t"] = 102.0

        result_a = get_normalized_weights(w_a)
        result_b = get_normalized_weights(w_b)

        for key in result_a:
            assert result_a[key] == pytest.approx(result_b[key], abs=1e-9), \
                f"Weights should be translation-invariant for '{key}'"

    def test_no_side_effects(self, biased_weights):
        """get_normalized_weights does not modify the weights instance."""
        logits_before = dict(biased_weights.logits)
        lr_before = biased_weights.learning_rate
        uc_before = biased_weights.update_count

        _ = get_normalized_weights(biased_weights)

        assert biased_weights.logits == logits_before, "Logits must not change"
        assert biased_weights.learning_rate == lr_before
        assert biased_weights.update_count == uc_before

    def test_four_equal_logits_quarter_each(self):
        """4 strategies at logit 0.0 each get weight 0.25."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(
            strategy_names=["a", "b", "c", "d"]
        )
        result = get_normalized_weights(w)
        for key, val in result.items():
            assert val == pytest.approx(0.25, abs=1e-9), \
                f"Expected 0.25 for '{key}', got {val}"

class TestComputeWeightedEmbeddingSimilarity:
    """Tests for compute_weighted_embedding_similarity."""

    def test_identical_vectors_similarity_one(self):
        """Identical unit vectors yield similarity 1.0."""
        result = compute_weighted_embedding_similarity(

            context_prototypes={"semantic": [0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0]},

        delta_sum = sum(result.logit_deltas.values())
        assert delta_sum == pytest.approx(0.0, abs=1e-10), \
            f"Zero-sum invariant violated: sum = {delta_sum}"

    def test_learning_rate_decay(self):
        """Effective learning rate decays as lr / (1 + update_count * 0.01)."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(
            strategy_names=["semantic"], learning_rate=0.05
        )
        # Manually set update_count to 100 to test decay
        w.update_count = 100
        contributions = {"semantic": 0.5}
        result = record_acceptance(w, contributions)
        expected_lr = 0.05 / (1 + 100 * 0.01)  # 0.05 / 2.0 = 0.025
        assert result.effective_learning_rate == pytest.approx(expected_lr, abs=1e-10), \
            f"Expected effective lr {expected_lr}, got {result.effective_learning_rate}"

    def test_new_strategy_inserted(self):
        """Strategies in contributions but not in logits are inserted with default 0.0."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(strategy_names=["semantic"])
        w.logits["semantic"] = 0.5
        contributions = {"semantic": 0.8, "technical": 0.6}
        result = record_acceptance(w, contributions)
        assert "semantic" in result.weights.logits
        assert "technical" in result.weights.logits, \
            "New strategy 'technical' should be inserted into logits"

    def test_in_place_mutation(self, uniform_weights):
        """record_acceptance mutates in-place and returns same object reference."""
        contributions = {"semantic": 0.5, "technical": 0.5, "social": 0.5}
        result = record_acceptance(uniform_weights, contributions)
        assert result.weights is uniform_weights, \
            "Returned weights must be the same object (in-place mutation)"

    def test_deltas_shrink_over_successive_updates(self):
        """After many updates, delta magnitudes decrease (ART stability)."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(
            strategy_names=["semantic", "technical"], learning_rate=0.1
        )
        contributions = {"semantic": 0.9, "technical": 0.1}

        # First update
        result_first = record_acceptance(w, contributions)
        first_max_delta = max(abs(d) for d in result_first.logit_deltas.values())

        # Run 200 more updates with the same contributions
        for _ in range(200):
            record_acceptance(w, contributions)

        # One more update to capture current delta magnitude
        result_late = record_acceptance(w, contributions)
        late_max_delta = max(abs(d) for d in result_late.logit_deltas.values())

        assert late_max_delta < first_max_delta, \
            f"Deltas should shrink: first={first_max_delta}, late={late_max_delta}"

    def test_update_count_monotonic(self):
        """update_count monotonically increases across multiple updates."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(strategy_names=["semantic"])
        contributions = {"semantic": 0.5}
        counts = []
        for _ in range(5):
            record_acceptance(w, contributions)
            counts.append(w.update_count)
        assert counts == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], \
            f"update_count should monotonically increase: {counts}"

    def test_logits_remain_finite_after_many_updates(self):
        """All logit values remain finite after many updates."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(
            strategy_names=["semantic", "technical", "social"],
            learning_rate=0.5,
        )
        contributions = {"semantic": 1.0, "technical": 0.0, "social": 0.5}
        for _ in range(500):
            result = record_acceptance(w, contributions)
        for key, val in result.weights.logits.items():
            assert math.isfinite(val), \
                f"Logit for '{key}' is not finite: {val}"

    # --- Error cases ---

    def test_error_empty_contributions(self, uniform_weights):
        """Raises ValueError when strategy_contributions is empty."""
        with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc_info:
            record_acceptance(uniform_weights, {})
        msg = str(exc_info.value).lower()
        assert "non-empty" in msg or "empty" in msg

    def test_error_nan_contribution(self, uniform_weights):
        """Raises ValueError when a contribution value is NaN."""
        with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc_info:
            record_acceptance(
                uniform_weights, {"semantic": float("nan")}
            )
        msg = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "finite" in msg.lower() or "Non-finite" in msg or "nan" in msg.lower()

    def test_error_inf_contribution(self, uniform_weights):
        """Raises ValueError when a contribution value is Inf."""
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            record_acceptance(
                uniform_weights, {"semantic": float("inf")}
            )

class TestEnsureStrategiesPresent:
    """Tests for ensure_strategies_present."""

    def test_adds_missing_strategies(self):
        """Missing strategies are added with default logit 0.0; existing unchanged."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(strategy_names=["semantic"])
        w.logits["semantic"] = 1.0
        result = ensure_strategies_present(
            w, ["semantic", "technical", "social"]
        )
        assert result.logits["semantic"] == 1.0, \
            "Existing logit should be unchanged"
        assert result.logits["technical"] == 0.0, \
            "Missing strategy 'technical' should be inserted at 0.0"
        assert result.logits["social"] == 0.0, \
            "Missing strategy 'social' should be inserted at 0.0"

    def test_idempotent(self):
        """Calling twice with the same strategies yields identical logits."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(strategy_names=["semantic"])
        w.logits["semantic"] = 2.0
        ensure_strategies_present(w, ["semantic", "technical"])
        logits_after_first = dict(w.logits)
        ensure_strategies_present(w, ["semantic", "technical"])
        logits_after_second = dict(w.logits)
        assert logits_after_first == logits_after_second, \
            "Idempotent: second call should not change logits"

    def test_returns_same_reference(self):
        """Returns the same object (in-place mutation)."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(strategy_names=["semantic"])
        result = ensure_strategies_present(w, ["technical"])
        assert result is w, \
            "ensure_strategies_present should return the same object reference"

    def test_preserves_all_existing_logits(self):
        """All pre-existing logit values are preserved, not just checked strategies."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(
            strategy_names=["semantic", "technical"]
        )
        w.logits["semantic"] = 3.0
        w.logits["technical"] = -1.5
        ensure_strategies_present(w, ["social"])
        assert w.logits["semantic"] == 3.0
        assert w.logits["technical"] == -1.5
        assert w.logits["social"] == 0.0

    def test_error_empty_strategy_name(self):
        """Raises ValueError when a strategy name is empty string."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(strategy_names=["semantic"])
        with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc_info:
            ensure_strategies_present(w, ["semantic", ""])
        msg = str(exc_info.value).lower()
        assert "non-empty" in msg or "empty" in msg

class TestSerialization:
    """Tests for serialize_dimension_weights and deserialize_dimension_weights."""

    def test_serialize_basic(self):
        """Serialized dict has correct keys and values."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(
            strategy_names=["semantic", "technical"], learning_rate=0.05
        )
        w.logits["semantic"] = 1.5
        w.logits["technical"] = -0.3
        w.update_count = 10
        # Manually set update_count for serialization test
        result = serialize_dimension_weights(w)
        assert result["logits"]["semantic"] == 1.5
        assert result["logits"]["technical"] == -0.3
        assert result["learning_rate"] == 0.05
        assert result["update_count"] == 10

    def test_serialize_json_compatible(self, biased_weights):
        """Serialized output is JSON-serializable."""
        result = serialize_dimension_weights(biased_weights)
        try:
            json_str = json.dumps(result)
        except (TypeError, ValueError) as e:
            pytest.fail(f"Serialized output is not JSON-compatible: {e}")
        assert isinstance(json_str, str)

    def test_serialize_empty_logits(self, empty_weights):
        """Serialization works with empty logits dict."""
        result = serialize_dimension_weights(empty_weights)
        assert result["logits"] == {} or len(result["logits"]) == 0

    def test_deserialize_full_data(self):
        """Deserialization with complete data restores all fields correctly."""
        data = {
            "logits": {"semantic": 1.5, "technical": -0.3},
            "learning_rate": 0.1,
            "update_count": 5,
        }
        result = deserialize_dimension_weights(data)
        assert result.logits["semantic"] == pytest.approx(1.5)
        assert result.logits["technical"] == pytest.approx(-0.3)
        assert result.learning_rate == pytest.approx(0.1)
        assert result.update_count == 5

    def test_deserialize_defaults(self):
        """Deserialization with only logits uses defaults for other fields."""
        data = {"logits": {"semantic": 0.0}}
        result = deserialize_dimension_weights(data)
        assert result.learning_rate == pytest.approx(0.05), \
            "Default learning_rate should be 0.05"
        assert result.update_count == 0, \
            "Default update_count should be 0"

    def test_roundtrip_serialization(self, biased_weights):
        """deserialize(serialize(w)) produces an equivalent instance."""
        biased_weights.update_count = 42
        serialized = serialize_dimension_weights(biased_weights)
        restored = deserialize_dimension_weights(serialized)
        assert restored.logits == biased_weights.logits, \
            f"Logits mismatch: {restored.logits} != {biased_weights.logits}"
        assert restored.learning_rate == pytest.approx(biased_weights.learning_rate)
        assert restored.update_count == biased_weights.update_count

    def test_roundtrip_empty_logits(self, empty_weights):
        """Round-trip works with empty logits."""
        serialized = serialize_dimension_weights(empty_weights)
        restored = deserialize_dimension_weights(serialized)
        assert restored.logits == empty_weights.logits
        assert restored.learning_rate == pytest.approx(empty_weights.learning_rate)
        assert restored.update_count == empty_weights.update_count

    # --- Deserialization error cases ---

    def test_deserialize_error_missing_logits(self):
        """Raises error when 'logits' key is missing from data."""
        with pytest.raises((ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, Exception)):
            # Contract says ValidationError — most implementations use pydantic
            deserialize_dimension_weights({"learning_rate": 0.05})

    def test_deserialize_error_nan_logit(self):
        """Raises error when a logit value is NaN."""
        with pytest.raises((ValueError, Exception)):
            deserialize_dimension_weights(
                {"logits": {"semantic": float("nan")}}
            )

    def test_deserialize_error_inf_logit(self):
        """Raises error when a logit value is Inf."""
        with pytest.raises((ValueError, Exception)):
            deserialize_dimension_weights(
                {"logits": {"semantic": float("inf")}}
            )

    def test_deserialize_error_invalid_learning_rate(self):
        """Raises error when learning_rate is out of (0.0, 1.0]."""
        with pytest.raises((ValueError, Exception)):
            deserialize_dimension_weights(
                {"logits": {}, "learning_rate": -0.5}
            )

    def test_deserialize_error_negative_update_count(self):
        """Raises error when update_count is negative."""
        with pytest.raises((ValueError, Exception)):
            deserialize_dimension_weights(
                {"logits": {}, "update_count": -1}
            )

    def test_deserialize_error_logits_not_dict(self):
        """Raises error when 'logits' is not a dict."""
        with pytest.raises((ValueError, TypeError, Exception)):
            deserialize_dimension_weights({"logits": [1.0, 2.0]})

class TestInvariants:
    """Cross-cutting invariant tests."""

    def test_softmax_sum_to_one_parametric(self):
        """Softmax weights always sum to 1.0 for various logit configurations."""
        configs = [
            {"a": 0.0, "b": 0.0},
            {"a": 10.0, "b": -10.0, "c": 0.0},
            {"x": 0.001, "y": -0.001},
            {"p": 100.0, "q": 100.0, "r": 100.0},
            {"solo": 42.0},
        ]
        for logits_dict in configs:
            w = initialize_dimension_weights(
                strategy_names=list(logits_dict.keys())
            )
            for k, v in logits_dict.items():
                w.logits[k] = v
            nw = get_normalized_weights(w)
            assert sum(nw.values()) == pytest.approx(1.0, abs=1e-9), \
                f"Weights must sum to 1.0 for logits {logits_dict}, got {sum(nw.values())}"

    def test_learning_rate_never_changes(self):
        """learning_rate is constant across updates."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(
            strategy_names=["semantic"], learning_rate=0.07
        )
        for _ in range(20):
            record_acceptance(w, {"semantic": 0.5})
        assert w.learning_rate == pytest.approx(0.07), \
            "learning_rate must never change after initialization"

    def test_effective_lr_formula(self):
        """Effective learning rate follows: lr / (1 + update_count * 0.01)."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(
            strategy_names=["semantic"], learning_rate=0.1
        )
        for i in range(10):
            expected_effective_lr = 0.1 / (1 + i * 0.01)
            result = record_acceptance(w, {"semantic": 0.5})
            assert result.effective_learning_rate == pytest.approx(
                expected_effective_lr, abs=1e-12
            ), f"At update {i}: expected {expected_effective_lr}, got {result.effective_learning_rate}"

    def test_empty_intersection_backward_compatible(self):
        """When strategy intersection is empty, similarity is 0.0 (backward compatible)."""
        result = compute_weighted_embedding_similarity(
            signal_embeddings={"semantic": [1.0, 0.0]},
            context_prototypes={"technical": [0.0, 1.0]},
            dimension_weights={"social": 1.0},
        )
        assert result.similarity == 0.0

    def test_missing_strategies_default_logit_zero(self):
        """Missing strategies are treated as logit 0.0 when requested via strategies param."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(strategy_names=["semantic"])
        w.logits["semantic"] = 0.0  # Explicitly set to 0.0
        # Request both semantic and technical; both at logit 0.0 should give equal weights
        result = get_normalized_weights(
            w, strategies=["semantic", "technical"]
        )
        assert result["semantic"] == pytest.approx(result["technical"], abs=1e-9), \
            "Both at logit 0.0 should have equal weights"

    def test_similarity_idempotent(self):
        """compute_weighted_embedding_similarity is idempotent (pure function)."""
        kwargs = dict(
            signal_embeddings={"semantic": [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]},
            context_prototypes={"semantic": [0.5, 0.5, 0.0]},
            dimension_weights={"semantic": 1.0},
        )
        result1 = compute_weighted_embedding_similarity(**kwargs)
        result2 = compute_weighted_embedding_similarity(**kwargs)
        assert result1.similarity == pytest.approx(result2.similarity, abs=1e-15), \
            "Pure function should return identical results on identical inputs"
        assert result1.strategies_used == result2.strategies_used

    def test_no_input_mutation_similarity(self):
        """compute_weighted_embedding_similarity does not modify its input arguments."""
        sig = {"semantic": [1.0, 0.0], "technical": [0.0, 1.0]}
        proto = {"semantic": [1.0, 0.0], "technical": [0.0, 1.0]}
        weights = {"semantic": 0.5, "technical": 0.5}

        sig_copy = {k: list(v) for k, v in sig.items()}
        proto_copy = {k: list(v) for k, v in proto.items()}
        weights_copy = dict(weights)

        compute_weighted_embedding_similarity(sig, proto, weights)

        assert sig == sig_copy, "signal_embeddings must not be modified"
        assert proto == proto_copy, "context_prototypes must not be modified"
        assert weights == weights_copy, "dimension_weights must not be modified"

    def test_logit_delta_direction(self):
        """Strategy with above-mean contribution gets positive delta, below-mean gets negative."""
        w = initialize_dimension_weights(
            strategy_names=["semantic", "technical"], learning_rate=0.1
        )
        # semantic contribution (0.9) > mean (0.5) → positive delta
        # technical contribution (0.1) < mean (0.5) → negative delta
        result = record_acceptance(
            w, {"semantic": 0.9, "technical": 0.1}
        )
        assert result.logit_deltas["semantic"] > 0, \
            "Above-mean contribution should yield positive delta"
        assert result.logit_deltas["technical"] < 0, \
            "Below-mean contribution should yield negative delta"
